title: Polyglot SDK operational contract: pagination, retry, and streaming behavior
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket captures the product requirements and acceptance criteria for a single operational contract across Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) for pagination, retry behavior, and streaming APIs. The goal is to define deterministic, observable, and backwards-compatible behaviours SDK consumers can rely on when integrating Redwood inference endpoints.
background: Multiple SDKs currently differ subtly in: how they expose token/record pagination, default retry/backoff strategies, semantics of streaming chunk ordering and reconnection, and how they preserve backward compatibility when new parameters are introduced. These differences cause engineering friction for customers and internal docs maintenance. This PRD is intended to unify expectations and provide acceptance criteria for engineers implementing the SDK changes.
goals: 1) Define a single operational contract that all three SDKs implement for pagination tokens, retry policy defaults and overrides, and streaming message shapes. 2) Preserve backwards compatibility for the existing stable endpoints by providing opt-in toggles for new behaviors where required. 3) Provide clear acceptance criteria and tests that can be run by SDK teams and CI. 4) Ship docs, migration guides, and code samples for each language.
non_goals: 1) Rewriting the entire SDK idioms for each language; language idiomatic wrappers are allowed as long as contract is preserved. 2) Changing server-side pagination semantics; this ticket only changes SDK surface and client-side handling. 3) Redesigning the streaming protocol beyond what's necessary to standardize SDK behaviors.
requirements:
- Pagination: SDKs must provide a consistent high-level pagination helper that accepts page_size and optional page_token and returns an iterator/async-iterator/stream of items. Helpers must surface next_page_token and total_count when server returns them.
- Pagination token handling: Tokens must be treated as opaque strings (no parsing). SDKs must expose a stable API to pass through tokens unchanged and to expose them from responses.
- Streaming: Streaming APIs must deliver ordered deltas/messages as received from the server. SDKs must provide both a low-level stream event API and a higher-level convenience helper that yields complete chunks or reconstructed objects.
- Streaming reconnection: SDKs must not automatically re-connect on mid-stream network failures by default; reconnection must be explicit or opt-in via a configurable retry_on_stream_failure flag.
- Retries: Define a default retry policy for idempotent operations (GET/list/embeddings): exponential backoff with jitter, max_attempts=5, initial_delay=200ms, max_delay=2s. Non-idempotent operations (mutating or create-like endpoints) must default to no automatic retries. SDKs must allow customers to override with a pluggable RetryPolicy object.
- Error types: SDKs must normalize server-side transient errors to a standardized error class (e.g., TransientError) and permanent errors to PermanentError; language-specific class names are acceptable but inheritance and fields must be documented.
- Timeouts: SDKs must expose per-request timeout and a global default (default request timeout = 120s).
- Observability hooks: SDKs must emit hooks/callbacks for request lifecycle events (on_request_start, on_request_end, on_retry, on_backoff) and integrate with tracing metadata where possible.
- Backwards compatibility: Existing method names/parameters must keep prior behavior unless marked as deprecated. Any breaking change must be behind a major-version bump or explicit opt-in flag.
- Documentation: Provide migration guides for any opt-in behavior and examples in Python/TS/Go.
- Tests: Each language repo must include unit tests and interop integration tests validating the contract (see test_plan).
acceptance_criteria:
- All three SDKs expose a Pagination helper API with identical semantics documented in the cross-language contract doc.
- Pagination helper preserves opaque tokens verbatim and surfaces next_page_token when present.
- Streaming APIs in each SDK deliver messages in server order, and a higher-level aggregator helper reconstructs objects for convenience.
- Default retry policy is implemented and matches the configured parameters (initial_delay=200ms, max_delay=2s, max_attempts=5) for idempotent paths; non-idempotent paths do not retry by default.
- SDKs offer a configurable RetryPolicy object and a runtime flag to opt into stream auto-reconnect.
- Standardized error types are implemented and mapped from server HTTP codes and error payloads.
- Observability hooks are present and exercised by unit tests.
- Cross-language interop test run (integration harness) that scripts identical list/stream scenarios passes for Python, TS, and Go.
- No behavioral regressions in the SDK smoke tests for existing critical customers (we run current customer smoke suite).
- Documentation and migration guide published in docs.redwood.ai/sdk with code samples in each language.
- Security review completed and signed off for retry and reconnection changes (replay/duplicate request risk assessed).
scope_changes: During scoping we decided to: 1) Move automatic stream reconnection out of scope by default (opt-in only) due to replay/duplicate semantics for non-idempotent streams. 2) Keep server-side pagination format unchanged; SDK wrappers only. 3) Defer introducing a 'safe retry token' header (server work) to a follow-up ticket. 4) Add an explicit observability hook requirement after feedback from platform teams.
tradeoffs:
- Choosing opt-in stream reconnection reduces resilience on transient mobile networks for customers who don't opt in, but avoids surprising duplicate semantics.
- Enforcing a stricter retry policy reduces accidental duplicate executions but increases customer effort to opt-in where aggressive retries are desired.
- Normalizing error classes may hide some language-specific exception metadata; we require SDKs to preserve the raw response payload in a field for advanced users.
compatibility_matrix:
Python: synchronous iterator via .paginate() and async iterator via .paginate_async(); streaming via Response.stream() yields StreamEvent objects and convenience .reconstruct() to yield application objects.
TypeScript: pagination uses async iterable (for await) via paginate(), streaming returns EventEmitter-style stream and an async iterator helper.
Go: pagination provides Channel-based iterator and helper Paginate(ctx, params) that returns (chan Item, chan error); streaming yields a typed channel of StreamEvent and a helper function ReconstructStream(ctx).
All SDKs must document identical field names in returned objects for the core contract: item_id, created_at, next_page_token, total_count, and error.code, error.message. Token values treated as opaque strings in all languages.
rollout_plan: 1) Finalize contract doc and ship to SDK teams (week 1). 2) SDK implementers create language PRs that implement core behaviors behind feature flags (week 2-3). 3) Run cross-language interop test harness and customer smoke tests (week 4). 4) Toggle feature flags on for non-production users and gather telemetry (week 5). 5) Gradual rollout to all users and merge flags to default on release branch pending no regressions (week 6-7). 6) Publish migration guides and announce in release notes (week 8).
test_plan:
- Unit tests per SDK for pagination token passthrough, next_page_token exposure, and iterator termination.
- Integration tests against staging server that produces paginated responses with and without total_count.
- Streaming tests that validate ordered delivery, aggregator correctness, and behavior when network disconnects occur; test both default (no auto-reconnect) and opt-in reconnection.
- Retry tests injecting transient 5xx and network timeouts to verify backoff and attempt limits.
- Cross-language interop harness that runs identical scenarios against the same test server and asserts parity of outputs and error mappings.
- Smoke tests for top 10 enterprise customers (run by solutions engineering).
